question.prompt:
In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(\angle ABC=90^\circ\) and \(BA=BC=\sqrt2.\) Points \(P_1,\) \(P_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(P_{2024}\) lie on hypotenuse \(AC\) so that \(AP_1=P_1P_2\) \(=P_2P_3\) \(=\cdots\) \(=P_{2023}P_{2024}\) \(=P_{2024}C.\)

What is the length of the vector sum \[ \begin{aligned} &\vec{BP_1}+\vec{BP_2}+\vec{BP_3} \\ &\quad {}+\cdots+\vec{BP_{2024}}? \end{aligned} \]

solutions.title: Pair vectors about the midpoint
solutions.explanation:
Pair points that are equally far from the two ends of \(AC\). Let \(H\) be the midpoint of \(AC\). Equal spacing makes \(H\) the midpoint of \(P_iP_{2025-i}\), so
\[
\vec{HP_i}+\vec{HP_{2025-i}}=\vec{0}.
\]
Consequently, each pair of vectors has the same sum:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\vec{BP_i}+\vec{BP_{2025-i}}
&=(\vec{BH}+\vec{HP_i})
 +(\vec{BH}+\vec{HP_{2025-i}})\\
&=2\vec{BH}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking \(i=1,2,\ldots,1012\) pairs every point exactly once. Thus the total vector is
\[
1012\cdot2\vec{BH}=2024\vec{BH}.
\]
By the Pythagorean theorem,
\[
AC=\sqrt{(\sqrt2)^2+(\sqrt2)^2}=2.
\]
The median to the hypotenuse of a right triangle has half the hypotenuse's length, so \(BH=1\). Therefore the requested length is \(2024\cdot1=\boxed{2024}\), choice \(\text{D}\).

solutions.title: Sum coordinates of equally spaced points
